man.ls: ls [-a] [-l] [-h] [path] — directory listing. -a: hidden files dikhao, -l: long format (perms/owner/size), -h: human-readable sizes.
man.cd: cd [path] — directory change. cd .. parent, cd ~ home, cd - last dir.
man.cat: cat <file...> — file print karo. Multiple files join ho jaate hain. Bade files ke liye less/head/tail use karo.
man.grep: grep [-i] [-n] [-c] [-v] [-r] <pattern> [file] — text search. -i: case-insensitive, -n: line number, -c: count, -v: invert. File na do to stdin padhta hai.
man.find: find [path] [-name pattern] [-type f|d] [-perm nnn] — filesystem tree search. Example: find /home -name '*.txt' -type f
man.head: head [-n N] [file] — pehle N lines (default 10).
man.tail: tail [-n N] [file] — aakhri N lines (default 10). Live: tail -f file.
man.sort: sort [-r] [-n] [-u] [file] — lines sort. -r reverse, -n numeric, -u unique. uniq se pehle hamesha sort.
man.uniq: uniq [-c] [file] — adjacent duplicate lines collapse. Pehle sort karo warna kaam nahi karega!
man.cut: cut -d<delim> -f<N> [file] — fields extract. Example: cut -d, -f2 servers.csv
man.tr: tr <set1> <set2> — characters translate. tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' lowercase. 'tr -d' delete set.
man.sed: sed 's/pattern/replacement/' [file] — stream editor. Line-by-line transform. -e multiple scripts.
man.awk: awk '{print $1, $3}' [file] — field processor. $0 = full line, $N = field, NR = line number. BEGIN/END blocks.
man.jq: jq [filter] [file] — JSON processor. jq . = pretty print, jq .user[0].role = path extract. Security data processing ka core.
man.ps: ps aux — all processes (PID, USER, %CPU, CMD). Custom: ps -o pid,ppid,user,cmd ax
man.top: top — live process monitor. CPU/MEM sorted. q to quit (lab mein snapshot milta hai).
man.df: df [-h] — filesystem space usage per mount.
man.du: du [-sh] [path] — actual directory/file sizes. du -sh * = top-level sizes.
man.ip: ip addr | ip route | ip neigh | ip link — interfaces, routes, neighbors. ifconfig/route ka modern replacement.
man.ss: ss -tlnp — listening TCP sockets + owning process. ss -tan — all TCP connections + states.
man.ping: ping [-c N] <host> — ICMP reachability test. LAB RULE: sirf lab.local / localhost allowed (Red Line).
man.dig: dig <host> [A|MX|TXT] — DNS query. +short = concise, +trace = full resolution journey.
man.host: host <name> — simple DNS lookup. host -t MX example.com = mail records.
man.curl: curl [-i] [-v] [-X METHOD] [-H header] [-d data] <url> — HTTP client. -i: headers dikhao. LAB RULE: sirf http://lab.local/* aur localhost:8080.
man.nmap: nmap [opts] <target> — network discovery (ports/services). LAB RULE: sirf lab.local. External target = RED LINE violation.
man.tcpdump: tcpdump [-i any] <filter> — packet capture. -n: no DNS resolve, -c N: N packets. LAB RULE: lab traffic only.
man.strace: strace [-p <pid>] [cmd] — system calls trace. -c: summary, -e trace=openat: filter. Permission/network debugging ka weapon.
man.lsof: lsof [-i :port] [-p <pid>] [-u user] — list open files. lsof -i :8080 = kaun us port pe hai. lsof +L1 = deleted-but-open files.
man.journalctl: journalctl [-u unit] [-n N] [--since '10 min ago'] [-p err] — systemd journal logs. Log investigation ka core tool.
man.systemctl: systemctl start|stop|restart|status|enable <unit> — services manage. daemon-reload config change ke baad.
man.ssh: ssh [-i key] user@host — encrypted remote shell. ssh-keygen -t ed25519 keys banata hai.
man.man: man <topic> — manual pages padho. Available: ls cd cat grep find head tail sort uniq cut tr wc sed awk jq ps top free df du ip ss ping dig host curl nmap tcpdump strace lsof journalctl systemctl chmod chown ssh man

i: Linux ek open-source monolithic kernel hai jo hardware ko manage karta hai — processes, memory, files, network sab iske through. GNU tools + Linux kernel milkar GNU/Linux OS banta hai.
Kernel hardware ke saath user-space ke beech ka bridge hai: process scheduling, memory management, device drivers, system calls. uname -r se version milta hai.
Distribution = kernel + packages + package manager + default configs ka bundle. Ubuntu (apt), Fedora (dnf), Arch (pacman) — sab alag distros, same kernel family.
Kernel (Linus Torvalds) + user tools jaise bash, grep, coreutils (GNU project) milkar poora OS banta hai. Isliye technically sahi naam 'GNU/Linux' hai.
Kernel space (ring 0) mein direct hardware access hai; user space (ring 3) mein aapke apps chalte hain. Isolation isliye taaki app crash se system na toote. strace -c ls se dono ka interaction dekho.
Process = running program ka instance. Har process ka apna PID, address space, file descriptors. ps aux se live dekho.
Linux mein 'everything is a file' — disk, network socket, terminal, USB device, sab file interface se access hote hain (regular, device, FIFO, socket nodes).
Har process ke open resources ko numbers milte hain: 0=stdin, 1=stdout, 2=stderr. ls -l /proc/self/fd se apne shell ke FDs dekho.
Apps kernel se directly nahi baat kar sakte — syscalls (read, write, open, execve) ka use karte hain. strace -c ls se live syscall traffic dekho.
Shell (bash/zsh) aapke commands ko parse karke processes start karta hai. Ye OS nahi, ek user-space program hai. echo $SHELL se verify karo.
Terminal = interface jisse shell tak input/output hota hai (TTY/PTY). Purane CRT ka digital version; aaj Ctrl+Alt+T ya tmux/zellij.
Environment variables (PATH, HOME, USER...) har process ko config dete hain. env se dekho, export VAR=val se set karo — child processes tak jaate hain.
/proc = running kernel ka live view virtual files mein (processes, memory, network). /sys = devices/drivers ka view. cat /proc/cpuinfo, ls /sys/class/net try karo.
Layers: Hardware → kernel (drivers, scheduler, VFS, network stack) → system services (systemd, dbus) → user apps. Yahi layering Linux ke stable hone ki wajah hai.

Network dekho: ip addr aur ip route

lx.hi: Aapko Linux sirf commands ka collection nahi, balki ek complete operating-system architecture ke roop mein samajh aa gaya.
lx.en: You now understand Linux as an operating-system architecture rather than just a collection of commands.

i: Bash commands line-by-line parse aur execute karta hai. #!/bin/bash shebang se scripts bante hain; bash script.sh ya ./script.sh se chalte hain.
Shell line ko tokens karta hai, phir operators se split: pipe, redirect, background, keyword expansion. Debug ke liye set -x (xtrace) use karo.
Single quotes = literal (koi expansion nahi), double quotes = variables expand, $(...) = command substitution. echo '$HOME' vs echo "$HOME" difference dekho.
Backslash agle character ko literal banata hai: \, " aur ' — sab backslash se escape hote hain. echo "a\nb" se real line break milta hai.
Patterns: * (kuch bhi), ? (ek char), [abc] (character set). ls *.txt, ls [a-c]* try karo. Glob fail ho to output khali — nullglob se control hota hai.
Expansion ka order: brace {a,b} → tilde ~ → variables → command substitution. ls -l {/etc,/home} try karo.
$(cmd) — command run karke uska output text mein replace karo. echo $(date); nested bhi chalta hai: $(cat notes.txt | wc -l).
Shell se processes tak jaane wale key=value pairs. export MY_VAR=hi — child processes ko bhi dikhega. env | grep PATH se dekho.
alias ll='ls -la' se shortcut. Dhyaan: non-interactive scripts mein aliases expand nahi hote — uske liye functions use karo.
myfunc() { echo "hi $1"; } — reusable blocks with parameters. Scripts mein maintainability isi se aati hai.
Commands ki list: history, Ctrl+R se search, !123 se re-run. HISTSIZE/HISTFILE se control hota hai.
Terminal editing shortcuts: Ctrl+A (start), Ctrl+E (end), Ctrl+W (word delete), Ctrl+U (line delete), Ctrl+K (end tak delete).
stty size, clear, colors (escape sequences), tput. stty -a se poore terminal settings dekho.
Program ko input ka source (keyboard ya pipe). cat bina args ke stdin se padhta hai. grep x < file se file stdin ban jaati hai.
Default output stream (fd 1). command > out.txt ise file mein bhejta hai. Programs apna normal output isi par dete hain.
Error stream (fd 2) — stdout se alag taaki errors clean output se mix na hon. cmd 2> err.log chala kar dekho.
0/1/2 ke alawa extra FDs bhi: exec 3> log.txt se naya FD kholo. lsof -p $$ se process ke saare FDs dekho.
cmd1 | cmd2 — cmd1 ka stdout, cmd2 ko stdin. ps aux | grep ssh classic. set -o pipefail se har stage ka exit status matter kare.
<(cmd) / >(cmd) — process ko file jaisa treat karo. diff <(ls /) <(ls /tmp) — bina temp files ke compare.
cat <<EOF ... EOF — multi-line stdin. Scripts mein config/templates inline likhne ke liye perfect. <<-EOF leading tabs ignore karta hai.
cmd <<< "text" — single-line stdin. grep x <<< "abc axd" — quick inline test.
> overwrite, >> append, 2>&1 errors ko stdout mein merge. cmd > out.txt 2> err.log — classic split pattern.
$? = last command ka exit code (0=success, non-zero=fail). cmd1 && cmd2 (sirf success par) aur cmd1 || fallback.

lx.hi: Aap terminal mein confidently kaam kar sakte hain aur shell command ko Linux ke internal data flow ke saath samajh sakte hain.
lx.en: You can confidently operate the terminal and understand how shell commands interact through Linux data streams and processes.

i: Absolute /etc/passwd root se shuru; relative notes.txt current directory se. pwd + realpath file se verify karo.
Directory bhi file hai — sirf name→inode entries ki list. ls -l mein pehla character d hota hai.
Dot . se shuru hote files hidden hain. ls -a se dikhao. .bashrc, .ssh, .secret_note aise hi files hain.
Hard link = same inode ka doosra naam; symlink = target path point karne wala chhota file. ls -li se inodes compare karo.
rwx × user/group/others. chmod 750 file, ls -l se dekho. Ye access control ki first line of defense hai.
File ki info — size, owner, timestamps (atime/mtime/ctime), inode number. stat file se sab milta hai.
Filesystem ka unique number jo content + metadata point karta hai. Rename ho to inode wahi. ls -i, inode usage: df -i.
Directory ke andar name → inode number ki mapping hoti hai. find . -maxdepth 1 entries dikhata hai.
Same inode ke multiple names (same filesystem mein). ln file link banata hai. Data tab tak rehta hai jab tak koi link na ho.
ln -s target link — path store karta hai, target alag file. Broken symlink possible hai. readlink -f se resolve karo.
Directory jahan doosra filesystem attach hota hai. mount, findmnt, df -h se dekho. /boot, /home, USB sab mounts.
ext4, xfs, btrfs, tmpfs, procfs, sysfs. blkid + findmnt -o TARGET,FSTYPE se identify karo.
Running kernel ka live view — processes, memory, network stats. cat /proc/uptime try karo.
Devices aur drivers ka view — network interfaces, USB. cat /sys/class/net/eth0/address MAC dega.
Device nodes — hardware access ke file interfaces. ls -l /dev | head dekho.
Runtime state — PID files, sockets, boot-time info. Reboot par empty ho jaata hai. ls /run.
List files; -a hidden, -l long, -h human, -R recursive. ls -lah /etc.
Metadata: size, owner, perms, timestamps, inode. stat /etc/passwd.
Tree search + filters: find /home -name '*.txt' -type f. -mtime, -size +10M, -perm bhi.
Filesystems attach/detach. mount | grep /home current mounts.
Disk space per mount: df -h (space), df -i (inodes).
Actual sizes: du -sh * top-level, du -ah | sort -h | tail largest files.
Device ki fs type + UUID: blkid /dev/sda1.

lab.d: Investigate: unusual files, links, mounts. Pehla goal — /home/learner mein hidden file dhundo.

tasks.t: Hidden file dhundo: ls -a /home/learner (ya find se)
Us hidden file ko padho: cat /home/learner/.secret_note
Forensics: find se /home mein saare .txt files dhundo

lx.hi: Aap Linux filesystem ko surface level par nahi, balki inode, metadata, links aur mounts ke level par samajhte hain.
lx.en: You understand Linux filesystems beyond basic navigation, including inodes, metadata, links, mounts, and virtual filesystems.

i: User/Group identity numbers — files inhi numbers se verify hoti hain, usernames sirf display ke liye. id se apna dekho.
Har file ka ek owner + group. chown user:group file (root chahiye). ls -l mein dikhta hai.
Read (content), Write (modify), Execute (run / enter directory). Directory ke liye x = andar ja sakte ho.
r=4, w=2, x=1 → sum: 755 = rwxr-xr-x, 640 = rw-r-----. chmod 755 script.sh.
Permissions change — symbolic (chmod u+x f) ya octal (chmod 640 f). -R recursive.
Owner/group change (root only). chown -R user:group dir.
Naye files/dirs par default permissions ka mask. umask 022 → files 644, dirs 755. umask -S readable format.
Doosre user (default root) se commands. sudoers policy check hoti hai. sudo -l se apni allowed commands dekho.
File execute hone par owner ki privileges le leti hai (e.g. /usr/bin/passwd). SUID binaries = attack surface. find / -perm -4000 2>/dev/null.
File: group owner ki permissions; Directory: naye files usi group ke. find / -perm -2000.
Directory mein sirf apni file delete kar sakte ho (jaise /tmp). find / -perm -1000.
Standard permissions ke upar per-user/per-group access. setfacl -m u:bob:rwx file, getfacl file.
Files par metadata keys (security contexts etc.). getfattr -d file.
Root ke powers ko 38 chhote capabilities mein split (CAP_NET_ADMIN...). getcap /usr/bin/capsh — precise privilege control.
Ownership + permissions + capabilities + LSM (AppArmor/SELinux) — sab milkar decide karte hain kaun kya kar sakta hai. Misconfigured system lab se seekho.

lx.hi: Aap samajhte hain ki Linux mein "kaun kya access kar sakta hai" kaise decide hota hai.
lx.en: You understand how Linux determines who can access, execute, modify, or administer resources.

i: Process ID — running process ka unique number. echo $$ se apne shell ka PID.
Parent Process ID — kaun is process ko start kiya. ps -o pid,ppid,cmd -p $$.
Parent-child hierarchy. ps axjf se tree view.
FG = terminal block; cmd & se BG start, Ctrl+Z hold, bg resume, fg wapas.
Current shell ki jobs: jobs list, %1 se job reference.
Process events: SIGTERM (15) graceful kill, SIGKILL (9) force, SIGINT (2) = Ctrl+C. kill -15 <pid>.
R running, S sleeping, D uninterruptible (disk wait), Z zombie, T stopped. ps -o stat,comm ax.
Har process ka virtual dir: cmdline, status, fd/, environ. cat /proc/self/status try karo.
Isolated PID views — containers isi se kaam karte hain. lsns se dekho (root).
Process ke open files/sockets: ls -l /proc/self/fd, lsof -p $$.
Process ki env: cat /proc/self/environ (null-separated) — tr se readable banao.
Exit ho gaya par parent ne wait() nahi kiya — entry rehti hai. ps aux | awk '$8 ~ /Z/'. Cleanup = parent ka exit.
Parent mar gaya → systemd (PID 1) adopt kar leta hai. Problem nahi, but awareness chahiye.
CFS scheduler, nice values (-20..19). nice -n 10 cmd, renice se priority.
Per-process limits: memory, files, CPU. ulimit -a dekho.
Process snapshot: ps aux (everything), ps -ef, ps -o pid,ppid,user,cmd ax.
Live monitor — CPU/mem sorted. -u user filter.
Interactive colorized top — filters, kill, search.
Name se PID: pgrep -af python (full cmd), pgrep -x sshd exact.
Syscalls trace: strace -p <pid>, strace -c ls. Permission issues ka weapon.
Kaun file/port use kar raha: fuser 8080/tcp.

lab.d: Unknown process identify karo: kaun, parent kaun, kya kar raha. Port 8080 ke process ko dhundo.

tasks.t: Saare processes dekho: ps aux (ya ps ax)
Port 8080 kaun use kar raha? ss -tlnp (ya lsof -i :8080)
Apne shell ka /proc inspect karo: cat /proc/self/status

lx.hi: Aap Linux system ke andar chal rahe processes ko inspect aur troubleshoot kar sakte hain.
lx.en: You can inspect, understand, and troubleshoot running Linux processes and their relationships.

i: Background daemons (sshd, nginx...). systemctl list-units --type=service se inventory.
Init system (PID 1) — services, mounts, sockets, timers units ke roop mein. systemctl status sshd.
BIOS/UEFI → bootloader (GRUB) → kernel → initramfs → systemd → default target. systemd-analyze blame se slow boot.
Units ke groups — multi-user.target (servers), graphical.target (desktop). systemctl get-default.
systemd ka cron-like scheduling. systemctl list-timers.
journal + /var/log files. journalctl -u sshd -n 50 — recent unit logs.
Kaun kisse depend karti hai: systemctl list-dependencies sshd.
/etc/systemd/system/*.service — ExecStart, After=, WantedBy=. systemctl cat sshd se padho.
Unit mein: ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges=yes, User=nobody. systemd-analyze security sshd score dega.
After=/Wants=/Requires= — order aur auto-start. Circular deps = boot issues.
Emergency mode: systemctl rescue ya systemd.unit=emergency boot arg. Root password reset isi se.
Unit level: MemoryMax=, CPUQuota=. systemctl show sshd -p MemoryMax.
cron (crontab -e) ya systemd timers. * * * * * cmd syntax.
start/stop/restart/enable/disable/status. daemon-reload config change ke baad.
-u unit, -n N, --since '10 min ago', -p err. Log investigation ka core.
User scheduled tasks: crontab -e edit, crontab -l view.

lab.d: Observe → Diagnose → Root cause → Fix → Verify → Document. Lab host ke logs mein OOM kill + failed service dhundo.

tasks.t: Failed logins timeline: cat /var/log/auth.log | grep Failed

lx.hi: Aap Linux server ko operate, diagnose aur recover kar sakte hain.
lx.en: You can operate, diagnose, repair, and document Linux server environments.

i: 7-layer reference: Physical→DataLink→Network→Transport→Session→Presentation→Application. Troubleshooting mein layer-by-layer approach seekhoge.
Practical 4-layer: Network Access→Internet→Transport→Application. Real protocols isi ke upar chalte hain.
32-bit address (dotted quad). Private ranges: 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16. ip addr se apna dekho.
128-bit address — IPv4 exhaustion ki wajah se. ip -6 addr, typical prefix /64.
Network ko CIDR se chhote networks mein divide: /24 = 256 addresses. ip route show se apne subnets dekho.
Packet ka path — next-hop gateway decide karna. ip route get <ip> se path test karo (lab mein lab.local).
IP → MAC resolution local network mein. ip neigh cache dikhata hai. ARP spoofing = attack vector (sirf theory mein).
Control/error messages — ping isi par. Ping ka reply ICMP echo-request/reply hai.
Reliable, ordered, connection-oriented. Retransmissions + ACKs. Web traffic mostly TCP.
Fast, unreliable, connectionless — DNS, VoIP. ss -uap se UDP sockets dekho.
SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK (3-way). tcpdump -i any 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0' se dekho (lab traffic).
LISTEN, ESTABLISHED, TIME_WAIT, CLOSE_WAIT... ss -tan se dekho. TIME_WAIT bahut ho to server issue.
Client side ka temporary port (32768–60999). Har naye outbound connection ke liye naya port.
Network communication ka endpoint (IP:port + protocol). ss -tlnp — kaunsa process kaunse port pe.
Destination → interface/gateway mapping. ip route show, ip route get <ip>.
Max packet size per hop. Chhota MTU + DF flag = timeout issues. ping -M do -s 1472 se test.
Bade packet ko chhote pieces mein (IP level). tcpdump mein 'frag offset != 0' filter.
Domain → IP: resolver → root → TLD → authoritative. dig +trace se full journey dekho.
DNS results cache hote hain (OS + resolver), TTL expire par fresh query. resolvectl flush-caches.
Encrypted channel: handshake (certs, key exchange) → symmetric session. curl -v https:// se steps dekho.
ip addr, ip route, ip neigh, ip link — modern networking CLI (ifconfig/route ka replacement).
Sockets: ss -tlnp (listening + process), ss -tan (connections). netstat se faster.
ICMP reachability: ping -c 4 lab.local. Block ho to aage ki layers check karo.

i: Method + URL + Headers + optional body. curl -i http://lab.local/ se raw request/response dekho.

GET (read), POST (send/create), PUT (update), DELETE (remove), HEAD (headers only), OPTIONS (capabilities).
Metadata: Host, User-Agent, Accept, Cookie, Authorization... curl -vI se dekho. Security headers (HSTS, CSP) yahi se check hote hain.
Server → client ka state (Set-Cookie). Sessions isi se track hote hain. curl -c jar -b jar se manage karo.
301 permanent, 302 temporary, 307/308. curl -L follow karta hai. Open redirects = security issue.
2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error (401/403/404), 5xx server error. Bug hunting mein 403/404 patterns dhundo.

Swiss-army HTTP: -i headers, -v verbose, -X POST -d data, -H header, -o file. Lab ka #1 tool.
Downloads + recursion: wget -r -l 1 url. Bada content save karne ke liye.
Response dump → grep filter → sed clean → awk columns → jq JSON. curl -s url | jq .user.

Authorization: Basic (base64 — encrypted NAHI!), Bearer tokens, API keys. curl -u user:pass, curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer t'.

i: NAME=value set; $NAME expand; ${NAME:-default} fallback. Scripts mein set -u se unset use fail ho jaata hai.
if [ condition ]; then ... fi; [[ ]] bash-extended (regex, &&). [ -f file ] file checks.
for x in ...; do ...; done, while [ cond], until. Range: for i in {1..5}.
Reusable + parameters + return. local variables mat bhulo.
arr=(a b c), ${arr[0]}, ${#arr[@]} length. Associative: declare -A.
$1..$9, $@ saare, $# count, shift. getopts se -flags parse karo.

log(){ echo "[$(date -Iseconds)] $*"; } — timestamped output, >> log file 2>&1. Debugging ki bread & butter.
Numbers: [[ $x =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; paths: realpath -e. Untrusted input = injection risk — hamesha validate.
#!/usr/bin/env bash, POSIX-safe syntax. Alpine/Debian dono par chalna chahiye.

def f(a, b=1): return a+b — defaults, *args, **kwargs. Docstrings likho.
import os, json, subprocess, requests. Standard library + pip. pip install -r requirements.txt.
try/except/finally — specific exceptions catch karo (except FileNotFoundError). Bare except = debugging death.
open('f') as f: f.read() — context manager (auto close). pathlib.Path modern way.
json.load(f), json.dumps(obj, indent=2). API work ka 90% isi se.
re.findall, re.search, re.sub — patterns se dhundo (emails, IPs, tokens).
subprocess.run(['ip','addr'], capture_output=True). shell=True avoid karo (injection risk).
requests.get(url) — status, json(), timeouts hamesha set karo. Web automation ka core.
Raw TCP/UDP: socket.socket(), bind/connect/send/recv. Custom protocols, scanners isi se.
concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor — parallel HTTP without raw threads ka complexity. Rate limit dhyan rakh kar.
logging module: levels (DEBUG..ERROR), formatters, file handlers. Ad-hoc print() se hamesha better.
argparse/typer — flags, subcommands, auto --help. Professional tooling.
Auth (tokens), pagination, retries (exponential backoff), error handling — real APIs isi se handle hote hain.
Chunked/line-by-line reading, generators — 10GB logs bhi process hote hain bina RAM exhaust kiye.

git diff (unstaged), git diff --staged, git diff HEAD~1. Code review culture isi par.

Release markers: git tag v1.0.0. SemVer: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
git remote -v, git push origin main, git pull. GitHub/GitLab connection.
Push NAHI karna: *.log, .env, __pycache__/. Secrets protect karne ka first step.
WIP commits squash karo, rebase se linear. Future-you ko thank you.

git checkout -- file (discard), git revert <sha> (safe inverse commit). Force push se bacho.
Fork/PR flow, code review, conventional commits. Team workflow.
README + docs ko code ke saath update karo. Doc drift = project death.

Code = repo, secrets = env vars / secret manager. .env.example provide karo, .env ignore.

Remote port ko local tunnel: ssh -L 8080:localhost:80 remote → local:8080 = remote's 80.
ssh-agent + ssh-add — private keys memory mein (with passphrase), multiple hops bina re-auth.
ProxyJump jump — intermediate host ke through auto tunnel. Bastion flows ke liye.
Single entry point internal network mein. Sab traffic yahan se — audit + control point.
Encrypted pipes: -L (local), -R (remote), -D (SOCKS). Insecure services ko tunnel se safe banao.
Key-only + 2FA + jump host + hardened sshd. Production level discipline.

Off by default, lock by default. Naya service? Pehle harden karo, phir production.
Root ke 38 powers ko split — sirf required capability do. capsh --print, setcap.
Isolated views (PID, NET, MNT, UTS...). Containers = namespaces + cgroups.
Resource limits (CPU, memory, IO) per group. systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=100M cmd.
Syscall filter — process ko allowed syscalls se ruko. Docker default se use karta hai.
Mandatory Access Control — user ki permissions se upar, kernel-level policy. DAC (rwx) se strong.
Ubuntu ka MAC — profile-based (per-app paths/capabilities). aa-status se dekho.
RHEL/Fedora ka MAC — labels + policy. getenforce, ausearch.

Read-only layered template (filesystem + config). docker pull, docker images.
Running instance of image. docker run -it --rm alpine sh.
Isolation (namespaces) + limits (cgroups) = container. Bina dono ke sirf 'chhota VM' nahi banta.
Union FS (layers) — base shared, top writable. docker history image se layers dekho.
docker build, -v mounts (persistent data), --network (isolation), -e env vars. Core operations.
Namespaces (visibility) + cgroups (resources) + seccomp (syscalls) + capabilities (privileges) — 4 lines of defense.

Non-root user, read-only fs (--read-only), no --privileged, network policies.
Small base (alpine/distroless), pinned versions, no secrets in layers, image scanning. Attack surface = image size.

App ke apne logs (access.log, app.log). Standard format: timestamp + level + message.
UTC vs local — timezone bugs forensic timeline todte hain. date -u, timedatectl.
Purane logs compress/archive (logrotate) — disk full + missing evidence dono se bachao.
Multiple logs ko timeline pe jodho: auth + app + network = full picture. awk se timestamp sort.
Kaunsa process kab chala: journal + /proc + history. journalctl _COMM=python.
conntrack, DNS queries, pcap — external activity ka proof. tcpdump -w se capture, baad mein analyze.
atime/mtime/ctime — file kab chhui/modified. stat, find -newer — timeline building.
New SUID binary, unknown cron, unusual port, off-hours root login, log deletion attempts. Baseline se deviation dhundo.
Kaun kya hold kar raha — open files/ports/processes.

i: In-scope assets ki written list — domain, IPs, endpoints, time window. Bina scope ke koi step illegal.
Apna lab: proxies, notes, data dirs, tool configs. Reproducible workspace = professional.
Subdomains, IPs, services, tech stack ka inventory. Structured data banta hai.
Subdomain enumeration, records (A, CNAME, TXT), old/unused assets dhundo — naya attack surface.
Headers, cookies, methods, redirects, status patterns. curl -sI batch mein — misconfigs surface hote hain.
Raw → normalize (lowercase, sort, dedupe) → structure (CSV/JSON). Unstructured data = no findings.
Auto-flag ko manually confirm — false positives kam karo. Har finding reproduce karo.
Screenshots + raw HTTP + timestamps + commands used. Evidence = proof of impact.
Title, severity, steps, impact, recommendation, evidence. Clear report = patched + paid.
Program scope ka legal document hai. 'api.example.com' vs '*.example.com' — difference huge. Pehla step hamesha scope.
Written permission (bug bounty program, contract). Red Line ke bina koi tool nahi.
Subdomains/assets categories mein: web, API, mobile, deprecated. Spreadsheet/DB maintain karo.
Commands consistent (aliases, scripts) — har run reproducible. history = audit trail.
Lowercase, trim, scheme add — duplicates detect hon. tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sort -u.
sort | uniq, awk '!seen[$0]++'. 10k raw → 1k unique. Time saver + cleaner report.
Har step ka output save: curl -s -i url > evidence/001.txt. Timestamp + context note.
3rd person aapke steps se same result de — commands + order + environment documented. Science, not magic.
Private disclosure, no public disclosure before fix, no data exfiltration. Trust = career.

i: Stages: input → validate → collect → normalize → dedupe → analyze → verify → report. Har stage isolated + testable.

Format standardize: lowercase, trim, scheme add. Har stage same shape = simple integration.
xargs -P / Python threads — bade lists fast. Rate limits + error handling ke saath, warna self-DoS.
Transient failures par backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s... for i in 1 2 3; do cmd && break; sleep 2; done.
Requests per second control — target ko mat todo, logs mein mat ghoomo. sleep 0.1 per request.
Har stage ka exit code check, failures log + report. Pipeline crash ≠ silent skip.
CSV/JSON/JSONL — human + machine readable. Downstream analysis isi par depend karta hai.

i: Logs (journalctl), core dumps, strace — kaunsi syscall fail hui. dmesg | tail se OOM killer check.
EACCES/EPERM — ownership, mode, capabilities, SELinux/AppArmor. stat file, getenforce, audit logs.
Layer by layer: interface → IP → route → DNS → port → service. ip, ip route, dig — har layer test.
systemctl status → journalctl -u → config → dependencies. 90% config ya resource issue.
top -P → kaunsa process → strace -c syscalls → code level. Thread vs process distinguish karo.
free -h, ps aux --sort=-%mem | head — leak? OOM? dmesg | grep -i oom.
df -h kaunsa fs → du -sh top dirs → deleted-but-open files (lsof +L1) → logs rotate.
State D? Zombie? ps -o stat,cmd -p pid → strace -p kya kar raha → open FDs (lsof).
Syscalls live trace — permission/network crashes ki root cause. -e filter, -c summary.
Open files/ports — 'kaun kya lock kar raha'. lsof -i :PORT, lsof +L1 deleted files.
Socket states — connection leaks, TIME_WAIT storm. ss -tan state time-wait | wc -l.
Service logs timeline — -u unit -S since. Failure ke exact time ka context.
Kernel ring buffer — hardware, OOM, I/O errors. dmesg -T timestamps ke saath.
Process state, CPU, mem — first step of almost every problem.
Crash post-mortem: core file load, backtrace, variables. gdb ./app core.1234 → bt.
Kya galat hai — user report/error message se shuru.
Logs, state, metrics collect karo — guess mat karo.
Controlled test se hypothesis verify/reject karo.
Dobara na ho — test case add karo.

i: User↔kernel ka sirf interface. strace -c frequency dekho. Kaunsa syscall slow/failed — performance + security dono.
Har process ko apna 48-bit address space — kernel pages ko physical RAM se map karta hai. Isolation + overcommit.
Text (code), data, heap, stack, mmap regions. cat /proc/self/maps layout dekho. Leaks yahan milte hain.
Open resources ka handle table — files, pipes, sockets. Limits: ulimit -n. Leak = FD exhaustion.
Network endpoints — kernel ka socket layer. ss -p kaunsa process. Buffer sizes, states — tuning.
Async events — kill, pause, segfault. kill -l list. trap (bash) / signal handlers (C).
CFS — fair time slices. Priority (nice), CPUQuota=. Latency-sensitive apps ke liye critical.
Syscalls (strace) + library calls (ltrace) + code level (gdb) — 3 layers of debug visibility.
ELF structure: headers, sections, symbols, dynamic entries. readelf -d lib dependencies.
Disassembly + sections. objdump -d machine code. Vulnerability research mein.
Symbols list (defined/undefined). nm -D lib.so — exported functions.
Printable text binary se — hardcoded paths, URLs, versions. strings /usr/bin/ls | grep -i key.
Linux executable format — headers + sections (.text, .data, .dynamic). file se type, readelf se detail.
Binary runtime mein libraries load karta hai. ldd /bin/ls — kaunsi libs.
.so files — memory sharing + updates. Versioning (libc.so.6). ld.so.preload = injection vector.
ld-linux.so — process start pe libraries find + map karta hai. LD_PRELOAD = powerful + dangerous.
Function/variable names — debugging + linking ke liye. Strip ho to symbols gayab → gdb mushkil.
Evidence-driven: reproduce → isolate → bisect → fix. Guesswork nahi, observation.

../ traversal, symlink attacks. realpath -e, base dir se resolve. Upload/download paths validate karo.
Predictable /tmp/name = symlink race. mktemp hamesha, mktemp -d dirs ke liye. sticky bit + permissions.
Env vars from secret files (600) ya secret managers. Git mein hardcode = compromised. Exposure par rotate.
set -euo pipefail, umask 077 scripts mein, no eval on input. Defense in depth in your scripts.

Profile collector, log filter, report generator.

toolCategories.title: 23.1 Linux Native Toolkit — built-in tools sabse pehle master karo
toolCategories.note: Mastery target: in commands ka PURPOSE aur COMBINATION samajhna chahiye — not necessarily every obscure flag memorize karna.

tools.name: grep
tools.errors: 'No such file' → path check; 'Binary file matches' → -a add karo
tools.integration: Pipelines ka core: cat f | grep x | wc -l; -o + cut + sort se structured output
tools.securityUse: Logs mein suspicious patterns, config audit, secret scan (grep -r 'password' .)

tools.name: find
tools.errors: 'Permission denied' → sudo ya 2>/dev/null; broad search slow → -maxdepth limit
tools.integration: find | xargs rm (careful!); find -exec stat {} ; metadata batch

tools.name: sed
tools.errors: 'unescaped newline' → escaping check; -i bina backup ke destructive
tools.integration: cat f | sed 's/://g' | sort -u; log parsing pipelines mein
tools.securityUse: Log sanitization (secrets redact karo), config normalize, pattern replace in reports

tools.name: awk
tools.errors: 'syntax error' → quotes check; -F galat → field positions shift
tools.integration: grep x f | awk '{print $5}' | sort | uniq -c — classic report pipeline
tools.securityUse: Log correlation (IP + timestamp + action extract), CSV → report, dedup with seen[]

tools.name: jq
tools.errors: 'parse error' → input valid JSON nahi; path miss → keys se structure dekho
tools.integration: curl -s url | jq .data — API work ka core; > file se save
tools.securityUse: API response analysis, user enumeration data clean, JSON logs parse, token structures inspect

tools.name: ss
tools.output: Socket list: state, local/peer addr, process
tools.errors: Empty → filter check; process column empty → sudo chahiye
tools.integration: ss -tlnp | grep :8080; ss -tan state time-wait | wc -l (leak detect)
tools.securityUse: Exposed services inventory (attack surface), connection states analyze, suspicious listeners

tools.name: ip
tools.errors: Permission → sudo (changes ke liye); empty route table → gateway check
tools.integration: ip addr | grep inet; ip route get <ip> (path trace); ip -j addr | jq (structured)
tools.securityUse: Interface audit, IP config verify, neighbor table (ARP anomalies), attack surface base

tools.name: curl
tools.errors: '(7) Failed to connect' → service down/DNS; '(6) Could not resolve' → DNS; '(35) SSL error' → cert
tools.integration: curl -s url | jq . (API); curl -o file url (download); loops se batch
tools.securityUse: Endpoint enumeration, auth testing (Bearer/Basic), redirect chains, cookie flags, error handling inspect

tools.name: dig
tools.errors: 'SERVFAIL' → server issue; 'NXDOMAIN' → domain exist nahi; timeout → resolver
tools.integration: dig +short domain; dig +trace domain (resolution journey); loops se subdomain check
tools.securityUse: Subdomain recon, TXT records (SPF/DMARC), DNS enumeration, stale records dhundo

tools.name: tcpdump
tools.errors: 'no permission' → sudo; 'no such device' → interface name; chup → filter galat
tools.integration: tcpdump -w cap.pcap & (background); baad mein Wireshark mein open; -A se HTTP payload
tools.securityUse: Packet forensics, protocol behavior verify, handshake/redirect observe, evidence capture (lab)

tools.name: nmap
tools.errors: 'Permission denied (UDP)' → sudo; timeout → target down; rate limit → --max-rate
tools.integration: nmap -oN scan.txt lab.local; grep open scan.txt; report mein use
tools.securityUse: AUTHORIZED targets only: service discovery, attack surface inventory, lab enumeration. External = RED LINE.

tools.name: strace
tools.errors: 'Operation not permitted' → sudo (other users' processes); 'attach: ptrace' → kernel restriction
tools.integration: strace -c cmd (performance); strace -e trace=network cmd (network syscalls); logs ke saath correlate
tools.securityUse: Permission errors root cause, network behavior trace, malware behavior (lab), crash diagnosis

tools.name: journalctl
tools.errors: 'No journal files' → systemd journal enabled nahi; empty → filter too specific
tools.integration: journalctl -u X -p err --since '1 hour ago' | grep pattern; > file se evidence
tools.securityUse: Service failure diagnosis, auth events timeline, failure correlation, incident response

certification.title: HOST READY — Linux Security & Bug Hunting
certification.hi: Aapko ek unfamiliar Linux host diya ja sakta hai. Aap system ko systematically understand, troubleshoot, automate aur authorized security lab ke context mein investigate kar sakte hain. Aap unfamiliar commands ke liye documentation use kar sakte hain aur bina blind copy-paste ke problem solve kar sakte hain.
certification.en: You can work on an unfamiliar Linux host, systematically understand and troubleshoot the system, automate routine tasks, and investigate authorized security-lab environments. You can use documentation to learn unfamiliar commands and solve problems without blindly relying on copy-paste instructions.

goldenRule.hi: Mastery tab hai jab learner ko pata ho problem kya hai, evidence kaha milega, kaunsa tool choose karna hai, output ka meaning kya hai, aur result ko independently verify kaise karna hai.
goldenRule.en: Mastery means knowing what the problem is, where to find evidence, which tool to choose, how to interpret its output, and how to independently verify the result.
